No plan yet — talk it through with J.A.R.V.I.S., then hit "Update Plan" to have him summarize where things stand.
J.A.R.V.I.S. tries each engine in order until one answers. Put a free-tier key in PRIMARY_API_KEY and paid models become the safety net rather than the meter; add FALLBACK_API_KEY_2 and _3 so one daily quota running out is not the end of the day. Press TEST ENGINES — better to find out here than mid-sentence.
Remote MCP servers J.A.R.V.I.S. can call — component libraries, design tools, anything that speaks MCP. Point these at your own worker's /mcp/name path so the API key stays server-side.
Leave empty to use the direct Anthropic connection, which only works while this file runs inside Claude chat. Once you deploy the jarvis-worker.js backend, paste its URL here so J.A.R.V.I.S. works from anywhere this file is hosted.
A starting-point Voice ID is prefilled — pick any voice from your Cartesia library and paste its Voice ID here to override it. Without a key, the browser's built-in voice is used instead.
This is what you SPEAK, not what the interface is in — they used to be the same setting, so reading the app in Hebrew forced the microphone to expect Hebrew. Only used when transcription runs in the browser; with the worker connected, the language is detected automatically and this is ignored.
Grant once and the browser remembers it for this site, so he stops asking. On iPhone, add the page to your Home Screen first — Safari forgets permissions for ordinary tabs every session.
Leave this on and the mic stays open — say his name and he answers. "Jarvis, what's on my calendar today" works in one breath; plain "Jarvis" arms him for whatever you say next. Costs battery, and needs mic permission plus a page that stays open.
